about: The book side of the chapter's proof steps: each step's lines in the proof (`book`, as export_annotations.find_proofs reads them), first words, title and note, and the relation of a step that no Lean carries out. The Lean side, which lines carry out a step and how, is in the `-- cite … step` markers.

steps.title: x = (x₁, …, xₙ) and y = (y₁, …, yₙ) in 𝐅ⁿ
steps.note: Binders `x y : Fin n → F`; the coordinates xₖ, yₖ are `x i`, `y i`.

steps.title: x + y = (x₁ + y₁, …) = (y₁ + x₁, …) = y + x
steps.note: `funext i` passes to coordinates. `(x + y) i` is `x i + y i` by definition (2nd, 4th equalities), so `add_comm (x i) (y i)`, the 3rd, closes the goal.

steps.title: Two additive identities 0 and 0′ of V
steps.note: Only 0′ is arbitrary: `z` with `h : ∀ v, v + z = v`. The other identity is mathlib's fixed `0`, whose law `add_zero` comes with the `AddCommGroup` instance.

steps.title: 0′ = 0′ + 0 = 0 + 0′ = 0, so the identity is unique
steps.note: `add_zero`, `add_comm` and `h 0` justify the three equalities, as in the book. The calc proves the goal `z = 0` for every `z` satisfying `h`, which is the uniqueness.

steps.title: Two additive inverses w and w′ of v
steps.note: Only w is arbitrary: `w` with `h : v + w = 0`. The other inverse, w′, is mathlib's `-v`, whose law v + (−v) = 0 is `add_neg_cancel`.

steps.title: w = w + 0 = w + (v + w′) = (w + v) + w′ = 0 + w′ = w′
steps.note: `h` is v + w = 0, the definition's order, so line 129 turns w + v into v + w by `add_comm`, a swap the book leaves implicit. The calc proves the goal `w = -v`.

steps.title: 0v = (0 + 0)v = 0v + 0v
steps.note: `rw [add_zero]` gives 0 = 0 + 0 in 𝐅; `add_smul` is the distributive property.

steps.title: Add −0v to both sides: 0 = 0v
steps.note: `congrArg` adds −0v to both sides of `h`; the `rw` chain spells out the simplification to 0 = 0v; `h2.symm` flips it.

steps.title: a0 = a(0 + 0) = a0 + a0
steps.note: `rw [add_zero]` gives 0 = 0 + 0 in V; `smul_add` is the distributive property.

steps.title: Add −a0 to both sides: 0 = a0
steps.note: `congrArg` adds −a0 to both sides of `h`; the `rw` chain spells out the simplification to 0 = a0; `h2.symm` flips it.

steps.title: v + (−1)v = 1v + (−1)v = (1 + (−1))v = 0v = 0
steps.note: `one_smul`, `add_smul`, `ring` on 1 + (−1) = 0, then `zero_smul'` (1.30).

steps.title: (−1)v is the additive inverse −v of v
steps.note: `unique_neg` (1.27) turns v + (−1)v = 0 into (−1)v = −v; the book's "the additive inverse" rests on that uniqueness.

steps.title: A subspace satisfies the three conditions
steps.note: `recall` restates mathlib's `Submodule.zero_mem`, `add_mem`, `smul_mem`. A `Submodule` has the three conditions as its fields, so no appeal to the vector-space axioms is needed.

steps.title: 0 ∈ U gives U the additive identity of V
steps.note: The three conditions are the binders `h0`, `hadd`, `hsmul` on S : Set V; `subZero` is ⟨0, h0⟩, the zero of V as an element of the subtype ↥S.

steps.starts: 𝑉 is in 𝑈. The second condition
steps.title: Closure under + makes addition land in U
Closure under scalars makes au land in U
−u = (−1)u ∈ U, so U has additive inverses
steps.note: `hsmul (-1)` gives (−1)u ∈ S and `simpa` rewrites (−1)u to −u (1.32); `sub_neg_add_cancel` checks (−u) + u = 0 in ↥S.

steps.title: The other axioms hold in U because they hold in V
steps.note: One theorem per axiom on ↥S; each is `Subtype.ext` applied to the same axiom of V (`add_assoc`, `add_comm`, `one_smul`, …).

steps.title: U is a vector space, hence a subspace of V
steps.note: Lean proves the axioms one by one and never assembles them into a `Module F ↥S` or a `Submodule`; in mathlib the three conditions are the fields of `Submodule`.

steps.title: V₁ + ⋯ + Vₘ is a subspace, by 1.34
steps.note: The sum is `U ⊔ W : Submodule F V`, a subspace by its type; the comment at lines 368–369 says so.

steps.starts: The subspaces 𝑉₁, … , 𝑉ₘ are all
steps.title: Each Vₖ ⊆ V₁ + ⋯ + Vₘ: the other summands are 0
steps.note: Two summands U, W only. u = u + 0 and w = 0 + w are the witnesses for `Submodule.mem_sup`, giving U ≤ U ⊔ W and W ≤ U ⊔ W.

steps.title: A subspace containing every Vₖ contains the sum
steps.note: Two summands U, W only. `mem_sup` writes x = y + z with y ∈ U, z ∈ W; `h₁`, `h₂` put y, z in X and `X.add_mem` puts y + z in X.

steps.title: V₁ + ⋯ + Vₘ is the smallest such subspace
steps.note: Lean leaves the two halves as separate examples; that U ⊔ W is the least upper bound of U and W is what `⊔` means in mathlib's lattice of submodules.

steps.title: Direct sum ⇒ 0 = v₁ + ⋯ + vₘ only with all vₖ = 0
steps.note: `h u 0` applies the definition to u and the zero family; `simpa` reads ∑ 0 as 0. The converse u = 0 → ∑ uᵢ = 0, which Lean's `↔` adds, is `simp`.

steps.title: Two representations v = v₁ + ⋯ + vₘ = u₁ + ⋯ + uₘ
steps.note: `IsDirectSum` says two families with equal sums are equal, so `intro h u v huv` takes the hypothesis and both representations at once. Lean's u, v are the book's v, u.

steps.starts: where 𝑢₁ ∈ 𝑉₁, … , 𝑢ₘ ∈ 𝑉ₘ. Subtracting
steps.title: Subtracting: 0 = (v₁ − u₁) + ⋯ + (vₘ − uₘ)
steps.note: `Finset.sum_sub_distrib` splits ∑ (u − v)ᵢ into ∑ uᵢ − ∑ vᵢ; `huv` and `sub_self` make it 0.

steps.title: vₖ − uₖ ∈ Vₖ, so the hypothesis makes each 0
steps.note: vₖ − uₖ ∈ Vₖ is built in: `u - v` is a family of subspace elements, so `(h _).mp` applies to it directly.

steps.title: Hence v₁ = u₁, …, vₘ = uₘ
steps.note: `sub_eq_zero` turns u − v = 0 into u = v for the whole family.

steps.title: v ∈ U ∩ W gives 0 = v + (−v)
steps.note: Lean packs v ∈ U and −v ∈ W (`W.neg_mem`) into a family u over Fin 2; `hsum` is ∑ uᵢ = 0, proved by `simp` with `Fin.sum_univ_two` from v + (−v) = 0.

steps.title: Unique representation of 0 gives v = 0, so U ∩ W = {0}
steps.note: Line 604 puts `h` in 1.45's form and turns U ⊓ W = ⊥ into ∀ v ∈ U ⊓ W, v = 0. `(h u).mp` gives u = 0; reading off u 0 gives v = 0.

steps.title: Suppose U ∩ W = {0} and 0 = u + w
steps.note: `hint` is U ⊓ W = ⊥ as ∀ v ∈ U ⊓ W, v = 0. The family u has u 0 ∈ U, u 1 ∈ W; `Fin.sum_univ_two` makes `hsum` read u 0 + u 1 = 0.

steps.title: By 1.45 it suffices to show u = w = 0
steps.note: `rw [isDirectSum_iff]` applies 1.45 once, before the split into the two directions.

steps.title: u = −w ∈ W, so u ∈ U ∩ W and u = 0
w = 0 by the equation, completing the proof
steps.note: `h1Z` gets w = 0 from u = −w and u = 0; `funext`, `fin_cases` and `Subtype.ext` assemble the family u = 0.
